note: The SOC 2 control catalog: every control that maps to a Trust Services Criterion, each marked operated only when current evidence shows it running and passing (statusRule), and not-yet-operated with the stated gap otherwise. A control whose evidence is collected names the collector keys in scripts/compliance/collect-soc2-evidence.mjs; a manual one says what the founder keeps by hand. scripts/check-soc2-controls.mjs fails on an unknown criterion, an unknown or unreferenced collector, a missing implementation path, a not-yet-operated entry with no gap, or a cycle 1 scope that disagrees with the criteria a control cites. The runbook is docs/runbooks/soc2-evidence.md, and audit/flows/soc2-readiness-2026-10-18.md is the readiness assessment the statuses were reconciled against. This file is not a SOC 2 report and claims no certification; docs/compliance/README.md rule 4 still applies.
statusRule: A control is operated only when it runs today and current evidence shows it passing. Built, documented or designed is not operated. The evidence dates below are from the 2026-10-18 pack (.cache/soc2-evidence/2026-10-18T225759Z, not committed) and from the production observations in audit/flows/soc2-readiness-2026-10-18.md.

framework.name: 2017 Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy (With Revised Points of Focus, 2022)
framework.verification: The AICPA download requires an account, so the 61 identifiers below were checked against intuitem's machine-readable copy of the same document (ciso-assistant-community, backend/library/libraries/soc2_2017_with_rev_2022.yaml), which packages the processing integrity criteria as PP1.1 to PP1.5; the AICPA numbering PI1.1 to PI1.5 is used here. The 2022 revision changed points of focus only, not the criteria. Titles are paraphrased, not the AICPA text.

scope.decision: Cycle 1 is Security plus Confidentiality, as audit/flows/soc2-readiness-2026-10-18.md recommends. Availability, Processing Integrity and Privacy controls stay listed so their gaps remain visible, marked out of scope for cycle 1. Availability returns in cycle 2 once RPO and RTO are declared and a timed production-like restore is on record. The founder and the CPA firm confirm scope in the engagement letter.
scope.soc1: Not proposed. A SOC 1 covers controls relevant to a customer's financial reporting, and nothing here processes a customer's financial records; Stripe billing is a subprocessor. The change, access and operations controls below are the IT general controls a SOC 1 would reuse if a customer ever asks for one.

ownersNote: AGI Automation LLC has one person. Every role below is held by the founder; the role names match docs/compliance/trust-claims.json so a future hire can take one over without renaming controls.

controls.title: Every production change is a commit on the main branch
controls.description: Code, configuration, migrations and workflows reach production only from git history on the GitHub default branch. The pack lists every commit in the period with its author and whether it arrived through a pull request.
controls.gap: Production cannot be traced to main. The last 10 production deployments (2026-10-16 to 2026-10-18) were created from the Vercel CLI with empty git metadata, and the 2026-10-18 pack lists 30 production deployments in the period with no commit SHA on any. main has no branch protection or ruleset (CM-05), so what reaches main is not gated either. Operates once every production deployment names the main commit it was built from.

controls.title: The guard chain runs before every push
controls.description: The pre-push hook runs check:llm-operability in a clean worktree of the commit being pushed, so lint, security, boundary, migration and documentation guards gate each push. SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 bypasses it, so the hook is a preventive control the operator can override; CI (CM-03) is the detective control behind it.
controls.gap: No run of the hook is on record. It can be skipped with SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1, and the 2026-10-18 pack attached no guard log because none is kept. CI on main failed on 58 of 126 pushed commits in the same period, so a passing pre-push run cannot be assumed. Operates once each month's pack attaches a passing --guard-log and pushes stop arriving red.

controls.title: CI runs on every push to main and its result is kept
controls.description: ci.yml runs the guard chain, lint, typecheck, affected tests and builds on every push to main. The pack records each pushed head commit with the conclusion of every workflow that ran on it.
controls.gap: CI runs but does not pass and does not gate. The 2026-10-18 pack shows 42 success, 58 failure and 24 cancelled verdicts over 126 pushed commits on main, and nothing stops a red commit: there is no required check (CM-05) and deployments do not depend on CI (CM-01).

controls.title: A second person approves a change before it merges
controls.description: Changes to main are reviewed and approved by someone other than their author.
controls.gap: There is one person, and commits are pushed straight to main. The main-history collector measures how many commits in the period arrived through an approved pull request. Until a second reviewer exists, CM-02 and CM-03 are the compensating controls and the auditor will report the lack of segregation of duties.

controls.title: Branch protection enforces the required check on main
controls.description: GitHub refuses deletion, force pushes and merges without the CI complete check on main.
controls.gap: .github/rulesets/main.json declares the intended ruleset, but GitHub reported no branch protection and no ruleset on main when this catalog was written. The branch-protection collector compares what GitHub enforces with the declared file on every run, so the day it is applied the pack shows it.

controls.title: Only the founder starts a production deployment
controls.description: Git-triggered deployments are off (vercel.json git.deploymentEnabled is false), so a merge never deploys. Production deploys are started by the founder, from the Vercel CLI or the founder-gated deploy-production workflow. The pack lists every production deployment in the period with its creator, state and creation time. A CLI deployment carries no commit SHA, so linking a deployment to the commit it built is a manual step.
controls.manualEvidence: For each production deployment in the period, the commit it was built from, noted at deploy time.
controls.gap: Every production deployment in the 2026-10-18 pack was created by siddharthanagula3, but the control's manual record, the commit each deployment was built from, has never been kept. Who else could deploy is not known: the Vercel member list was unavailable without VERCEL_TOKEN, and the team is a personal one named after the founder. deploy-production.yml is disabled_manually, so the founder-gated workflow path does not run.

controls.title: Database changes go through the append-only migration chain
controls.description: Schema changes are numbered, checksummed migrations under apps/web/db/neon that are never edited after they apply. Production apply needs --confirm-production, the applied point is recorded in scripts/config/production-migrations-applied.json, and a Neon branch is cut before each production apply.
controls.manualEvidence: The migrate command output for each production apply in the period.

controls.title: Dependency updates are proposed weekly
controls.description: Dependabot opens version and security update pull requests on a weekly schedule for every ecosystem the repository uses, and GitHub security updates are enabled. The pack counts the Dependabot pull requests opened in the period and how each ended.

controls.title: Infrastructure access is reviewed monthly
controls.description: Each month the founder reviews who holds access to GitHub, Vercel and Neon, and at what level, and removes what is not needed.
controls.gap: No access review has been recorded. The collectors list the population each month; the review becomes operated when the founder signs the access section of a pack, as the runbook describes.

controls.title: Multi-factor authentication on every infrastructure account
controls.description: Every account that can reach source, deployments or the production database signs in with a second factor.
controls.gap: Neon reported has_mfa false for its only organization admin when this catalog was written. GitHub exposes two-factor status only to a classic token with user scope, and Vercel does not expose it at all, so those two need a dashboard screenshot.

controls.title: Product data access is scoped to its owner
controls.description: Every route and service that reaches a user-owned table through the owner connection is constrained to the requesting owner or declared and allowlisted, and every tenant table carries an explicit isolation decision. The pack reruns those guards. Production cannot yet be shown to run the tested commit (CM-01), so this evidences the code, not the deployment.

controls.title: Support access to customer data needs a customer grant
controls.description: Operator access to a workspace's data requires a grant the workspace issues, and every grant and its use is written to a hash-chained trail the workspace can read.
controls.manualEvidence: An export of the support access grant trail for the period from the production database, or a statement that it is empty.
controls.gap: The grant needs one operator to request and a second to approve, and there is one operator, so it cannot operate as designed (readiness assessment, CC6.3). No grant export has been collected.

controls.title: Secrets stay out of source control
controls.description: The working-tree secret scan runs in the guard chain, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled on the repository. The pack reruns the scan and records open secret-scanning alert counts, never their values.

controls.title: Stored credentials are encrypted under a rotating key ring
controls.description: Connector, GitHub installation and TOTP secrets are encrypted at rest under keys on a 12-month rotation calendar with a rehearsal script. Nothing rotates itself; the rotation is a calendar obligation.
controls.manualEvidence: The rotation record (date, key, reencrypt sweep output) for any rotation that fell due in the period; the next due date is 2027-08-17.
controls.gap: Encryption at rest is in the code, but nothing in a pack shows it running in production, the first scheduled rotation is not due until 2027-08-17, and the keys exist only as deployment variables with no escrow (docs/security/security.md section 3, accepted risk).

controls.title: Personnel access is granted and removed with employment
controls.description: Joiners receive access only after authorisation, and leavers lose it on their last day.
controls.gap: There are no employees or contractors with access. The first hire needs a written onboarding and offboarding checklist before access is granted.

controls.title: Physical security is inherited from the hosting providers
controls.description: No company-operated facility holds production data; the providers' data centres do.
controls.gap: Carving out the physical criteria to the subservice organizations needs their SOC 2 reports on file and complementary controls named. No vendor report has been collected yet (VM-02).

controls.title: Production health and error budgets page a human
controls.description: Vercel crons probe health every ten minutes, evaluate SLO burn twice an hour and page security anomalies every fifteen minutes through the one incident dispatcher.
controls.manualEvidence: The pager history for the period, exported from the alert destination the dispatcher writes to.
controls.gap: No detector reaches a human. Production logged incident_paging disabled (PAGER_WEBHOOK_URL not set), error_reporting disabled (no Sentry DSN), tracing_export disabled and transactional_email disabled (Resend not configured) on 2026-10-18, deployment dpl_AYcoWbw9pPHbyEMVABQTb1DdyTm7, per the readiness assessment. The crons in vercel.json run with no channel to page.

controls.title: Scheduled security, drift and drill workflows run and are watched
controls.description: CodeQL, Trivy and the web container DAST, environment drift reconciliation, the restore drill and the container portability drill run on schedules. The pack records every scheduled workflow, whether GitHub has it enabled, and each run's conclusion in the period.
controls.gap: The workflows run, but failures are not reviewed and are not rare. In the 2026-10-18 pack, security-scanning had 21 failures, codeql-analysis 9, env-drift 8 failures and 92 cancellations, and deploy-production is disabled. No record shows anyone read a red run, and production paging is off (OP-01). Operates once failures are reviewed in the monthly pack.

controls.title: Dependencies are audited for known vulnerabilities
controls.description: CI fails on critical JavaScript advisories, and the pack records the full pnpm and cargo advisory audit at collection time.

controls.title: Security incidents follow the incident response runbook
controls.description: Detected incidents are triaged, contained, recovered and written up with the postmortem template. A personal data breach follows its own runbook, which is a draft that counsel has not reviewed.
controls.manualEvidence: Each incident record and postmortem opened in the period, or a signed statement that there were none.
controls.gap: Never exercised: no incident has been declared, the breach runbook has not been reviewed by counsel, and detection cannot reach a human (OP-01), so the response procedure has no trigger in production.

controls.title: Known defects are tracked by severity until fixed
controls.description: Every unfixed defect has a row in the known flaws register with a severity, cited by ID from CI and tests, and deleted when fixed. The pack counts open rows by severity.
controls.manualEvidence: None beyond the register; its git history shows when each row opened and closed.

controls.title: Production database point-in-time history and pre-change branches
controls.description: Neon keeps point-in-time history for the production project, and a branch or snapshot is cut before each production migration. The pack records the retention window, the branch list, snapshots and backup schedule.
controls.gap: Point-in-time history on the production project is 6 hours (history_retention_seconds 21600, 2026-10-18 pack), too short to recover from a problem noticed the next day. The default branch is not protected, the backup schedule is empty, and object storage backup is not provisioned (readiness assessment).

controls.title: Database restore is drilled weekly
controls.description: db-restore-drill.yml restores a point-in-time branch and verifies it every week. The pack records each drill run and its conclusion.
controls.gap: The scheduled drill failed four weeks running, 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-12, before two manual successes on 2026-10-13. The 2026-10-18 pack shows 2 successes and 4 failures for db-restore-drill.yml in the period.

controls.title: Continuity, rollback and vendor exit plans are maintained
controls.description: Business continuity, release rollback and vendor migration runbooks state what can be recovered, how and in what order. The pack records each file's digest and last commit so a change to a plan is visible.
controls.manualEvidence: An annual sign-off that the plans were read against the current system.
controls.gap: The plans are written, but no annual sign-off has been made, and no RPO or RTO is declared for them to be read against.

controls.title: Capacity is measured against a stated target
controls.description: Load is tested against the capacity target and the result is kept.
controls.gap: AGENTS.md section 8 forbids claiming the capacity target without a live run, and no live load run is on record.

controls.title: Public trust claims are re-reviewed within 90 days
controls.description: Every row of the public trust ledger names an owner, the paths that make it true and an executable proof, and check:trust-claims fails a review older than the cadence. The pack lists each row's review date and age. The proofs run against the repository, not against production configuration.

controls.title: Published policies are versioned and dated
controls.description: Terms, privacy, DPA, security and every other policy page print a last-updated date from one constant, each version is recorded and archived, and check:policy-versions fails when the page and the record disagree.

controls.title: Security policy and procedures are written down
controls.description: The security document and the runbooks state how access, keys, retention, incidents and recovery are handled, and the repository contract makes the guards that enforce them mandatory.
controls.manualEvidence: An annual sign-off that docs/security/security.md was reviewed.
controls.gap: docs/security/security.md and the runbooks are procedures, not an approved, dated and owned policy set, and no review sign-off exists. The readiness assessment lists the missing policies under CC5.3.

controls.title: A formal risk assessment is done each year
controls.description: Risks to objectives, including fraud and significant change, are identified, rated and given a response.
controls.gap: The known flaws register tracks defects, not business risk. No dated risk assessment covering fraud and change exists.

controls.title: Governance oversight of internal control
controls.description: Someone independent of day-to-day operation oversees internal control, and structures and responsibilities are written down.
controls.gap: A single-member LLC has no board. The usual answer is a documented annual management review, which has not been held.

controls.title: A code of conduct is acknowledged
controls.description: Everyone with access acknowledges a code of conduct and acceptable use policy, and breaches carry consequences.
controls.gap: The public acceptable use policy binds customers, not staff. No internal code of conduct exists.

controls.title: Security awareness training each year
controls.description: Everyone with access completes security awareness training on joining and each year.
controls.gap: No training record exists, including for the founder.

controls.title: The monthly evidence pack is reviewed and signed
controls.description: Each month the founder runs the evidence collector, reads the summary, records exceptions and signs it.
controls.gap: The collector is new; no pack has been signed. The first signed pack starts the record a Type 2 observation period needs.

controls.title: Subprocessors are listed publicly and kept complete
controls.description: /subprocessors names every vendor that receives customer data, a change moves its date and is announced, and check:subprocessor-coverage fails when a provider the registry admits for managed traffic is missing. The pack records the published list.

controls.title: Vendor assurance reports and DPAs are reviewed each year
controls.description: Each subprocessor's SOC 2 or ISO report and data processing terms are obtained, read and filed, and complementary user entity controls are noted.
controls.gap: No vendor report or signed DPA is on file for review.

controls.title: Erasure and retention reach every store, and holds stop them
controls.description: check:retention-graph fails when a store holding a subject reference is not reached by erasure, and check:legal-hold-coverage fails when a destructive statement is not gated by a hold. The pack reruns both.
controls.gap: The guards pass on the tree (2026-10-18 pack), but soft-deleted resources are never purged in production: apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-soft-deleted-resources/route.ts runs only when SOFT_DELETED_RESOURCE_PURGE_ENABLED is true, and production does not set it (readiness assessment), while the privacy policy promises a 30-day purge.

controls.title: Users can export and delete their data themselves
controls.description: Signed-in users request a full data export archive and account deletion from settings, and privacy requests have an endpoint. The export completeness and deletion route tests run in CI when those paths change.
controls.manualEvidence: A count of export, deletion and privacy requests received and completed in the period, from the production database.
controls.gap: The routes exist, but no count of requests has been collected, CI does not pass reliably (CM-03), and the export-ready mail cannot be sent because transactional email is disabled in production (readiness assessment).

controls.title: Processing integrity controls
controls.description: Inputs, processing, outputs and stored items are controlled for completeness and accuracy against stated specifications.
controls.gap: Processing integrity is not in the proposed scope, and no control has been designed against it.

controls.title: Privacy choice, consent, quality and disclosure accounting
controls.description: Choices and consent are communicated, collection and use stay within stated purposes, data is kept accurate, and disclosures are recorded and reportable to the data subject.
controls.gap: Privacy is not in the proposed scope. Parts may already be built, but none has been mapped and evidenced as a control.
